title: Production layout variations

location.series: Pentagram / The Public Theater case study

slide_intent: Separate fixed elements from variable placement because a flexible identity needs recognizable boundaries.
strategic_value: A repeated black frame and Public signature can connect varied titles and image positions.
demonstration: A three-by-three array compares framed layouts for A Play by William Shakespeare, Passing Strange and Macbeth in orange, blue and green.
practical_value: Compare nine placements to identify which elements can move while the family remains legible.

content_islands.name: Comparison grid
content_islands.spec: Arrange three production columns across three rows.

content_islands.name: Internal variation
content_islands.spec: Vary title position, color and image blocks within the heavy rectangular frames.

reference_purposes.Expression: A three-by-three array compares framed layouts for A Play by William Shakespeare, Passing Strange and Macbeth in orange, blue and green.
reference_purposes.Application: Nine worked layouts demonstrate alternative placements for three production titles within the same framed system.
reference_purposes.Intent: Pentagram says the updated system retains activity while adding structure through a grid and printer-like rules.

ingredient.name: Black frame and movable production blocks
ingredient.role: Keep varied compositions related while allowing different emphases.
ingredient.application: Compare the demonstrated placements inside the outer frame; vary title and image placement while retaining clear grouping.
ingredient.scope: Observed case-study alternatives, not an exhaustive template or mandatory placement system.
